newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Fotex to benefit from rising consumption.
newsitem.headline: Fotex to benefit from rising consumption.

text.p: Hungarian retail group Fotex, after reporting a strong profit gain on Friday, is set to reap further benefits from increasing domestic consumption, analysts said.
"The year 1998 will be stronger than 1997 (for Fotex)," said Andrea Dicso of Bank Austria Investment. "The (economic) growth will be higher, the population will have more money to spend."

Fotex, releasing its first-half IAS consolidated results, said its operating profits jumped to 608 million forints ($3.1 million) in the first six months of 1997 from 198 million in the same period of last year, while its net income was up to 390 million forints from 184 million.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Fotex shares closed at 236 forints, up three from Thursday's close but below the day's peak of 245 forints.

Analysts said the stock was undervalued and saw further growth potential both in its price and in the company's operation but said Fotex's track record in transparency and in relation to the investor community needs improvements.

"We think Fotex is very much undervalued," said Robert Feuer, analyst at WestMerchant. "Particularly if we consider that its results this year will probably well exceed last year's figures," he added. "I would not be suprised if its net income reached one billion forints."

Fotex's 14-day relative strength index (RSI) was at a neutral 54.86 percent level on Thursday. A share is regarded overbought if its RSI value is above 70 percent and oversold if its RSI is below 30 percent.

Feuer said that Fotex, hard hit by austerity measures launched in March 1995 with the aim of reducing Hungary's double deficits in budget and current account, has benefited from Hungary's economic revival.

"Due to this (austerity programme) many people delayed consumption but now consumption has started to pick up," Feuer said. "A real wage growth in the first half was clearly beneficial for retailers."
Average net real wages grew an inflation-adjusted 5.4 percent in January-June from a year ago, according to the Central Statistical Office's figures released this month.
Macroeconomic analysts expect Hungary's gross domestic product to grow by some three percent in 1997, driven by mainly by export growth, new investments and a recovery in consumption.

Bank Austria's Dicso said a substantial part of Fotex's profit stemmed from the fact that in 1997 it did not have the one-off group restructuring costs that reduced its profit by an estimated 160 million forints last year.
"The comparative base in 1996 was depressed and if we exclude this 160 million forints, the growth is not that impressive," Dicso said.

"The (beneficial) impact of last year's restructuring can be felt but we think most of the profit growth stems from the fact that this cost item did not come this year," she said, adding that Fotex's efficiency has grown.
